statement: At the Denisova Cave type site, Bayesian modeling of the fossils themselves dates the oldest Denisovan fossil to approximately 195,000 years ago and the youngest to 52,000-76,000 years ago (with Neanderthal fossils at the same site, including a first-generation Neanderthal-Denisovan hybrid individual, falling between 80,000-140,000 years ago). A separate sediment (environmental) ancient-DNA study extends the earliest attested Denisovan genetic signal at the site to approximately 250,000-170,000 years ago, associated with early Middle Palaeolithic tools, and documents a Denisovan mitochondrial-DNA population turnover after roughly 80,000 years ago.

sources.citation: Douka, K. et al. "Age estimates for hominin fossils and the onset of the Upper Palaeolithic at Denisova Cave." Nature 565: 640-644.
sources.author: Douka et al.

sources.author: Jacobs et al.

notes: Confidence set to MODERATE because the fossil-based range (195,000-52,000 ya) and the sediment-DNA-based range (up to ~250,000 ya) rest on different evidence types and should not be silently merged into one number when rendered — report both, sourced separately.
